purpose: Primary literature for CellPFN's procedural simulator as PFN training prior, its antecedents and boundaries; NBT Wave 1.
method: Targeted literature search, not systematic-review coverage. Web search discovery across publisher, PubMed, PMC, arXiv, CVF and OpenAlex records; retained claims grounded only in original papers or their author/publisher records. Metadata extracted into structured records and BibTeX rendered programmatically.

access_limitations: Direct Python urllib request to https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1186/s13059-017-1305-0 failed with temporary DNS resolution error. No Crossref API verification is claimed.
Several PMC opens returned CAPTCHA; publisher or indexed original full-text passages were used where available and recorded separately.
Final scMultiSim main text is subscription-only; retained claim is supported directly by final abstract and extended-data captions.
Full-paper reading is not claimed for every source; exact access level is recorded per entry.
DOIs for Wood 2021 and FlowNet 2015 were not independently verified and are intentionally omitted; their official CVF proceedings metadata is sufficient for identification.
metadata_decisions: scDesign3: 2024 issue year retained, with 2023 online date documented.
scMultiSim: final 2025 Nature Methods article replaces the 2023 preprint.
Wood: final CVF proceedings author list has six authors; later arXiv author list differs. Final proceedings list retained.
Duo: complete 14-author list taken from PMC; OpenAlex search extract listed a shortened set and historical strategy note wrongly used Liu et al.
Marouf: original article identifies first author as Matteo, correcting legacy Mohamed.
Crowell: compound surname Morillo Leonardo preserved; updated publisher article lists a 2024 correction.
Article-number journals use their article identifiers in pages for standard BibTeX compatibility.

sources.title: Splatter: simulation of single-cell RNA sequencing data
sources.author: Zappia, Luke and Phipson, Belinda and Oshlack, Alicia
sources.access: Full publisher HTML opened; Abstract, Background and Splatter framework inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Background; Results: The Splatter framework; Results: Splat
sources.claim: Splatter provides reproducible count simulation, including gamma–Poisson Splat, controlled populations and trajectories. Parameters may be estimated from data or supplied by the user.
sources.boundary: Do not describe all existing simulators as necessarily reference-dependent: Splatter explicitly permits default or user-supplied parameters. Its presence does not establish any CellPFN speed advantage.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Simulating multiple faceted variability in single cell RNA sequencing
sources.author: Zhang, Xiuwei and Xu, Chenling and Yosef, Nir
sources.access: Full publisher HTML opened; Abstract, Introduction and variability sections inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Introduction; Results: Allele intrinsic variation / Extrinsic variation / Technical variation
sources.claim: SymSim separates transcriptional stochasticity, cell-state variation and assay effects, with controls for discrete/continuous states and experimental steps.
sources.boundary: Explicit biological and technical randomization predates CellPFN. Cite as a foundation for controllable simulation, not as an inferior method without direct comparison.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {scDesign2}: a transparent simulator that generates high-fidelity single-cell gene expression count data with gene correlations captured
sources.author: Sun, Tianyi and Song, Dongyuan and Li, Wei Vivian and Li, Jingyi Jessica
sources.access: Full updated publisher HTML opened; Abstract and model overview inspected.
sources.anchor: Introduction: properties 4–6; Results: An overview of scDesign2
sources.claim: scDesign2 fits cell-type-specific count marginals and a Gaussian copula to real data, preserves gene correlations and permits different cell counts and sequencing depths.
sources.boundary: It also permits parameter adjustment; do not claim fitted models merely duplicate a fixed atlas. Publisher lists 2021 and 2023 corrections; use the updated article.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {scDesign3} generates realistic in silico data for multimodal single-cell and spatial omics
sources.author: Song, Dongyuan and Wang, Qingyang and Yan, Guanao and Liu, Tianyang and Sun, Tianyi and Li, Jingyi Jessica
sources.access: Publisher metadata and PubMed abstract verified; indexed PMC author-manuscript body/Fig. 1–2 extracts read. Direct PMC open encountered CAPTCHA.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Fig. 1 overview; Fig. 2 experimental-design examples
sources.claim: scDesign3 learns interpretable parameters from real data to simulate varied cell states, feature modalities and experimental designs, including spatial and multimodal settings.
sources.boundary: Do not claim that reference-fit methods lack adjustable batch effects or customized controls. Bibliographic year is the 2024 issue year; online publication was 11 May 2023.
sources.role: Core: modern flexible statistical simulator and NBT precedent.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {SERGIO}: A Single-Cell Expression Simulator Guided by Gene Regulatory Networks
sources.author: Dibaeinia, Payam and Sinha, Saurabh
sources.access: Indexed publisher and PMC full-text extracts read; direct publisher open failed and PMC open encountered CAPTCHA.
sources.anchor: Summary; Introduction; model description of stochastic transcription and user-specified GRNs
sources.claim: SERGIO uses specified regulatory networks and stochastic transcription to generate steady-state or differentiating single-cell expression with controlled noise.
sources.boundary: This is a mechanistic simulation precedent. CellPFN’s current prior must not be represented as a validated GRN-dynamics model merely because it includes correlated programs.
sources.role: Core or grouped citation: mechanistic simulation.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Spearheading future omics analyses using {dyngen}, a multi-modal simulator of single cells
sources.author: Cannoodt, Robrecht and Saelens, Wouter and Deconinck, Louise and Saeys, Yvan
sources.access: Full publisher HTML opened; Abstract and Introduction inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Introduction: three simulation stages; Fig. 1
sources.claim: dyngen translates regulatory networks into reactions, simulates cellular dynamics and emulates measurement protocols to benchmark trajectory, regulatory-network and RNA-velocity methods.
sources.boundary: Known latent truth and controllable simulation are established capabilities; the CellPFN distinction is the use of a prior for learning inference across tasks.
sources.role: Core or grouped citation: dynamics and mechanistic ground truth.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {scMultiSim}: simulation of single-cell multi-omics and spatial data guided by gene regulatory networks and cell--cell interactions
sources.author: Li, Hechen and Zhang, Ziqi and Squires, Michael and Chen, Xi and Zhang, Xiuwei
sources.access: Final publisher metadata, Abstract and extended-data captions opened; main final article subscription-only. Earlier PMC preprint indexed, not substituted for final-version claims.
sources.claim: scMultiSim combines cell identity, regulatory networks, cell–cell interactions, chromatin accessibility and technical noise while generating linked modalities.
sources.boundary: Use final 2025 Nature Methods record, not the historical 2023 preprint. Multimodal or spatial capabilities are context, not demonstrated CellPFN capabilities.
sources.role: Core or grouped citation: current broad simulator capabilities.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: The shaky foundations of simulating single-cell {RNA} sequencing data
sources.author: Crowell, Helena L. and Morillo Leonardo, Sarah X. and Soneson, Charlotte and Robinson, Mark D.
sources.access: Full updated publisher HTML opened; Abstract, Background and benchmark design inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract Conclusions; Background paragraphs on de novo/reference-based trade-offs; Benchmark design
sources.claim: The evaluation of 16 simulators found artifacts in complex designs, optimistic integration performance and potentially unreliable clustering rankings; summary similarity alone was not an established guarantee of valid comparisons.
sources.boundary: Supports caution and downstream validation, not a claim that no simulator can be useful. Distinguish their benchmarking question from training a PFN prior. Publisher lists a July 2024 correction.
sources.role: Core: reason to test transfer rather than infer usefulness from fidelity.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Systematic evaluation with practical guidelines for single-cell and spatially resolved transcriptomics data simulation under multiple scenarios
sources.author: Duo, Hongrui and Li, Yinghong and Lan, Yang and Tao, Jingxin and Yang, Qingxia and Xiao, Yingxue and Sun, Jing and Li, Lei and Nie, Xiner and Zhang, Xiaoxi and Liang, Guizhao and Liu, Mingwei and Hao, Youjin and Li, Bo
sources.access: Full PMC article opened; authors, Abstract, Background and Results framework inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract Results/Conclusions; Results: overall benchmark framework; Fig. 1
sources.claim: A benchmark of 49 methods across 152 reference datasets assessed accuracy, functionality, scalability and usability, finding trade-offs and no best method on every criterion.
sources.boundary: Its method accuracy measures resemblance under the evaluated scenarios; these do not directly measure PFN training utility. Cite Duo, not the incorrect Liu-led attribution in the old strategy note.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Fake It Till You Make It: Face Analysis in the Wild Using Synthetic Data Alone
sources.author: Wood, Erroll and Baltru{\v{s}}aitis, Tadas and Hewitt, Charlie and Dziadzio, Sebastian and Cashman, Thomas J. and Shotton, Jamie
sources.booktitle: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
sources.access: Indexed official CVF article/BibTeX and accepted-paper PDF page-one extracts read; direct HTML open failed.
sources.claim: Procedurally rendered faces train landmark and parsing models that transfer to real images, with label types that would be difficult or impossible to annotate manually.
sources.boundary: A precedent, not proof of CellPFN transfer. Use the six authors in the final CVF proceedings; the later arXiv record has a different author list. DOI not verified and omitted.
sources.role: Core short precedent for ground truth and synthetic-only learning.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Domain randomization for transferring deep neural networks from simulation to the real world
sources.author: Tobin, Josh and Fong, Rachel and Ray, Alex and Schneider, Jonas and Zaremba, Wojciech and Abbeel, Pieter
sources.booktitle: 2017 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
sources.access: IEEE indexed Abstract/DOI verified; arXiv author Abstract page opened. Main paper not fully inspected.
sources.claim: Randomizing simulated visual properties enabled an object-localization model to transfer to real robotic settings despite non-photorealistic textures.
sources.boundary: Motivates domain randomization; does not guarantee that arbitrary or larger biological randomization improves transfer. Proceedings pages not independently verified and omitted.
sources.role: Core short precedent for task-relevant domain randomization.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {FlowNet}: Learning Optical Flow With Convolutional Networks
sources.author: Dosovitskiy, Alexey and Fischer, Philipp and Ilg, Eddy and Hausser, Philip and Hazirbas, Caner and Golkov, Vladimir and van der Smagt, Patrick and Cremers, Daniel and Brox, Thomas
sources.booktitle: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
sources.access: Indexed official CVF article/BibTeX and accepted-paper PDF page-one extracts read; direct HTML open failed.
sources.claim: Flying Chairs supplied supervised optical-flow examples when available ground-truth data were insufficient; the trained networks generalized to other optical-flow datasets.
sources.boundary: Do not describe all evaluated datasets as real imagery: Sintel is synthetic, whereas KITTI supplies a real-world evaluation. DOI not verified and omitted.
sources.role: Reserve: one additional example if the simulator motivation needs it.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Realistic in silico generation and augmentation of single-cell {RNA}-seq data using generative adversarial networks
sources.author: Marouf, Matteo and Machart, Pierre and Bansal, Vikas and Kilian, Christoph and Magruder, Daniel S. and Krebs, Christian F. and Bonn, Stefan
sources.access: Full publisher HTML opened; Abstract, Introduction, conditional generation and Discussion inspected.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Results: Conditional generation of specific cell types; Discussion
sources.claim: cscGAN learns from measured multi-cell-type data to generate specified populations; augmentation improves analyses of sparse cell populations and classifier robustness.
sources.boundary: This is learned generation and augmentation from real observations, distinct from procedural-only parameter training. Do not imply prior single-cell simulation lacked downstream classification utility.
sources.role: Core: distinguish augmentation from the PFN-prior route.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {scDiffusion}: conditional generation of high-quality single-cell data using diffusion model
sources.author: Luo, Erpai and Hao, Minsheng and Wei, Lei and Zhang, Xuegong
sources.access: Indexed publisher full-text Methods extracts and PDF front matter read; direct HTML open failed.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Introduction final paragraphs; Section 2 Materials and methods / Fig. 1
sources.claim: scDiffusion uses a pretrained SCimilarity autoencoder, diffusion denoising and conditional guidance to generate expression under specified or combined conditions.
sources.boundary: Generation learns from real cell data and a pretrained foundation model. Cite for controlled neural generation, not synthetic-only pretraining without real-data-derived weights.
sources.role: Core or grouped citation: current learned synthetic generation.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression
sources.author: Squair, Jordan W. and Gautier, Matthieu and Kathe, Claudia and Anderson, Mark A. and James, Nicholas D. and Hutson, Thomas H. and Hudelle, R{\'e}mi and Qaiser, Taha and Matson, Kaya J. E. and Barraud, Quentin and Levine, Ariel J. and La Manno, Gioele and Skinnider, Michael A. and Courtine, Gr{\'e}goire
sources.access: Indexed publisher Abstract/Results/Discussion extracts and PubMed complete authors verified; direct publisher open failed.
sources.anchor: Abstract; Results: False discoveries in single-cell DE; Discussion
sources.claim: Between-biological-replicate variability matters for valid differential-expression inference, and treating cell observations as substitutes for replicate-aware inference can create false discoveries.
sources.boundary: This is evidence about differential expression, not a direct experiment on CellPFN or atlas-pretraining diversity. Use narrowly for donor-aware motivation or later Methods.
sources.role: Reserve: supports donor structure and independent biological units.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.

sources.title: {splatPop}: simulating population scale single-cell {RNA} sequencing data
sources.author: Azodi, Christina B. and Zappia, Luke and Oshlack, Alicia and McCarthy, Davis J.
sources.access: Full publisher HTML opened; Abstract and Background inspected; PubMed metadata cross-check.
sources.claim: splatPop already models population-scale expression with known eQTLs, batch/cell-group effects and conditional differences between individuals or cohorts.
sources.boundary: Donor/cohort-aware simulation is not novel by itself. CellPFN’s contribution should be the sampled task prior and its measured value for learning inference.
sources.role: Core or reserve: prevents overstating the novelty of donor-aware simulation.
sources.verification: Bibliographic identity and specified narrow claim checked against the cited primary source; access limitations retained.
